title: Render progressive Galaxy wheel zoom on the retained native path

scope.subject: Subdivide strong physical Galaxy wheel targets through the existing native render path without adding navigation, delaying input, or bypassing exact handoff.

research_summary: Real Chromium wheel on the #185 build turns one 120-pixel notch into an immediate 0 to 0.250 jump in the applied native scale. The existing YEIS path already supports continuous scrubbing and the renderer has its own delta and matched-endpoint signal. Reuse the installed Three.js MathUtils.damp inside that frame; the coordinator still owns input and boundaries. Compare camera-controls smoothing (wrong owner for the native Galaxy camera) and timed YEIS navigation (locks wheel and introduces two authorities).

sources.finding: Current pinned native renderer remains the authority; no upstream patch or new camera.
Installed MathUtils.damp interpolates using delta time with no internal queue or clock; pass the existing R3F frame delta.

search_ladder.conclusion: Keep the installed MIT YEIS and current camera entry/return behaviors; not a renderer replacement.
Keep the existing R3F Canvas and React phase state, no new scene or camera.
Keep the retained native YEIS bridge; existing camera-controls interpolates the separate close-world camera, not Galaxy.
Reuse MathUtils.damp on the existing native-applied coordinate; input target retains one owner.

candidates.name: Installed MathUtils.damp on the existing YEIS path
candidates.source: Installed Three.js MathUtils plus native Galaxy frame in YeisGalaxyScene
candidates.license: Project code plus existing MIT camera dependency
candidates.reason: Retarget from the currently rendered value every frame without changing path, boundaries, or producing a navigation request.

candidates.name: Use camera-controls or timed autopilot instead
candidates.source: Existing close-world CameraControls and native YEIS timed navigation
candidates.reason: Wrong camera owner or returns to autonomous travel; duplicates manual scale authority.

decision.rationale: Keep native YEIS camera, current scale target and matching; apply only a short interruptible visual response before native scrubbing.
decision.fallback: Retain #185 on main if real mouse progressive/reversal and native handoff checks are not green.
